**Issue #4981 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4981: Patch: WebSocket match, co-op and watch routes normalize match and profile UUIDs to lowercase, so uppercase hex connects to in-memory actors and seats
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
WebSocket connection handshakes for 1v1 matches (`/ws/match`), co-op matches (`/ws/duos`), and spectator watching (`/ws/watch`) will normalize query parameters and hello frame identifiers (`matchId` and `friendId`) to lowercase before performing in-memory actor lookups and seat authorization checks.

## Why
- In PostgreSQL, UUID columns format and compare in text representation as lowercase hexadecimal strings (`p1_profile_id::text`, `id::text`).
- REST endpoints throughout `crates/server` (such as `crates/server/src/social/mod.rs` `param()`, `crates/server/src/daily/invites.rs`, `crates/server/src/lobby/mod.rs`, `crates/server/src/social/challenges.rs`, and `crates/server/src/social/friends.rs`) explicitly normalize profile and match UUID parameters with `.to_ascii_lowercase()`. Furthermore, `crates/server/src/auth.rs`'s `is_uuid` explicitly tests and accepts uppercase 36-character hyphenated UUID strings (`67E55044-10B1-426F-9247-BB680E5FE0C8`).
- However, WebSocket entrypoints bypass REST parameter helpers and fail to normalize identifiers:
  1. `/ws/match` (`crates/server/src/actor/ws_server.rs:496-511`): `query_param(query, "matchId")` is kept as supplied. If a reconnecting player's URL contains uppercase hex, `profile.in_match_id.as_deref() != Some(match_id.as_str())` evaluates to true (since `profile.in_match_id` is loaded from the database in lowercase), and `seats_finished_match` returns `false` because the match is live. The server immediately refuses the connection with WebSocket close code 4403 ("you are not in that match").
  2. `/ws/watch` (`crates/server/src/social/watch.rs:68-88`): `parse_watch_hello` leaves `matchId` and `friendId` un-normalized. In `watchable_in` (`crates/server/src/social/watch.rs:419-421`), `seated(friend_id)` performs exact string equality `row.players.0 == id || row.players.1 == id` against database-loaded lowercase strings. Uppercase hex causes `seated` to evaluate to `false`, refusing spectators with 4403 (`NOT_ALLOWED`). Furthermore, `app.matches.attach_watcher` looks up the live actor in `app.matches` (`HashMap<String, MatchActor>`) keyed by lowercase database UUID, causing an in-memory lookup miss and failure.
  3. `/ws/duos` (`crates/server/src/duos/ws.rs:66` and `crates/server/src/duos/registry.rs:310-330`): `duos_hello` and `query_match_id` are not lowercased. In `registry.attach`, `self.get(match_id)` searches `self.actors` (`HashMap<String, DuosActor>`), which is keyed by lowercase UUIDs. When `match_id` has uppercase characters, the lookup misses the live running actor. Consequently, `self.actor_for` queries the store, replays the action history, and instantiates a duplicate in-memory actor for an already active match.

## Proposal
1. In `crates/server/src/actor/ws_server.rs`:
   - In `upgrade_socket`, normalize `query_param(query, "matchId").map(|id| id.to_ascii_lowercase())`.
2. In `crates/server/src/social/watch.rs`:
   - In `parse_watch_hello`, map `match_id` and `friend_id` via `.to_ascii_lowercase()`.
3. In `crates/server/src/duos/ws.rs`:
   - In `attach_socket`, normalize `asked` and `query_match_id` to lowercase using `.to_ascii_lowercase()`.
4. Add regression test cases in `crates/server/tests/api/match_socket.rs`, `crates/server/tests/api/watch.rs`, and `crates/server/tests/api/duos.rs` demonstrating that connecting with uppercase UUID parameters succeeds, attaches to existing in-memory actors, and admits spectators.

## Where it lands
- `crates/server/src/actor/ws_server.rs` (`upgrade_socket`)
- `crates/server/src/social/watch.rs` (`parse_watch_hello`)
- `crates/server/src/duos/ws.rs` (`attach_socket`, `duos_hello`)
- `crates/server/tests/` integration test suites for WebSocket matches, duos, and watching

## Acceptance criteria
- Connecting to `/ws/match?matchId=<UPPERCASE_UUID>` for a player in that live match connects and attaches to the existing live actor instead of closing with 4403.
- Sending a `hello` frame on `/ws/watch` with uppercase `matchId` and/or `friendId` successfully admits the watcher and attaches to the match actor instead of closing with 4403.
- Connecting to `/ws/duos` with uppercase `matchId` (in hello frame or query param) attaches to the existing in-memory `DuosActor` without triggering a redundant rebuild or duplicate actor creation.
- Existing lowercase connections continue to work unchanged.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server` passes with no regressions.

## Size and risks
- Size: Small. Less than 25 lines of production code across 3 files, plus targeted tests.
- Risks: None. UUID hex formatting is defined as case-insensitive by RFC 4122. Lowercasing on entry aligns WebSocket handling with existing REST routes in `crates/server`.

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45732119250)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

WebSocket handshakes for `/ws/match`, `/ws/duos`, and `/ws/watch` lowercase `matchId` (and `friendId` on watch) before any actor lookup or seat check, so an uppercase-hex identifier connects to the already-running in-memory actor instead of closing with 4403 or spawning a duplicate `DuosActor`. Lowercase clients behave exactly as before.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/server/src/actor/ws_server.rs` | change | `upgrade_socket`: lowercase the `matchId` query value |
| `crates/server/src/social/watch.rs` | change | `parse_watch_hello`: lowercase `match_id` and `friend_id`; new unit test in its `mod tests` |
| `crates/server/src/duos/ws.rs` | change | `attach_socket`: lowercase the resolved `match_id` |
| `crates/server/tests/actor/ws_server.rs` | change | new test: uppercase `?matchId=` attaches to the live 1v1 match |
| `crates/server/tests/actor/watch.rs` | change | new test in `mod b50_watching_a_friend`: uppercase hello admitted |
| `crates/server/tests/actor/duos.rs` | change | two new tests in `mod b35_the_socket`: uppercase hello id and uppercase `?matchId=` attach to the running actor |

Do not touch `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `spec/` (no ruling note: UUID case-insensitivity is RFC 4122 and REST routes already lowercase, so this aligns sockets with settled behavior rather than deciding anything new), `apps/web`, or any migration. Governing spec: S6 (duos socket), S7 (watch), §9.1/§9.4/§9.5 (match sockets, seat checks).

## Steps

1. In `crates/server/src/actor/ws_server.rs`, `upgrade_socket` (line 496), change `let asked = query_param(query, "matchId");` to `let asked = query_param(query, "matchId").map(|id| id.to_ascii_lowercase());`. Nothing else there: the `profile.in_match_id` fallback is already lowercase from the database, and the comparison, `seats_finished_match`, and `app.matches.attach` below then all run on the lowered value. Copy the pattern from `crates/server/src/social/mod.rs` `param()`, which lowercases the same way.
2. In `crates/server/src/social/watch.rs`, `parse_watch_hello` (lines 85-88), lowercase both ids at construction: replace `(Some(match_id), Some(friend_id)) => Ok(WatchHello { match_id, friend_id }),` with `Ok(WatchHello { match_id: match_id.to_ascii_lowercase(), friend_id: friend_id.to_ascii_lowercase() })`. Every downstream use (`may_watch`, `watchable_in`'s `seated` string equality, both `attach_watcher` calls keyed by lowercase database ids) then sees lowercase. Do not change `may_watch`/`watchable_in` themselves.
3. In `crates/server/src/duos/ws.rs`, `attach_socket` (lines 66-77), lowercase the resolved id once, covering the hello value, the `?matchId=` query value, and the `live_match_of` fallback (already lowercase; lowering is idempotent): after the `let match_id = match asked.or(query_match_id) { ... };` block and before `registry(app).attach(...)`, insert `let match_id = match_id.to_ascii_lowercase();`. No change is needed in `handle_duos` (`ws_server.rs:920`) or `duos_hello`: the single lowered binding feeds `registry.attach`, hence `get`/`actor_for`/`keep`, so no duplicate actor is registered under an uppercase key.
4. In `crates/server/src/social/watch.rs` `mod tests`, next to `a_hello_names_the_match_and_the_friend`, add `fn a_hello_with_uppercase_ids_is_read_lowercase` asserting `parse_watch_hello(r#"{"type":"hello","matchId":"67E55044-10B1-426F-9247-BB680E5FE0C8","friendId":"67E55044-10B1-426F-9247-BB680E5FE0C11"}"#)` equals `Ok(WatchHello { match_id: "67e55044-10b1-426f-9247-bb680e5fe0c8", friend_id: "67e55044-10b1-426f-9247-bb680e5fe0c11" })`.
5. In `crates/server/tests/actor/ws_server.rs`, add a new top-level `mod an_uppercase_match_id_in_the_query { use super::*; ... }` (the file's one-behavior-per-mod convention) with `async fn attaches_to_the_live_match_instead_of_refusing_with_4403`: lock `SERIAL`, `listen_with(1)`, then `open_as(listening.port, "MATCH-1", &tokens[0]).await.open()` and assert `first_view()["viewer"] == "p1"`. `"match-1".to_ascii_uppercase()` is `"MATCH-1"`, so this is non-vacuous; without the fix the socket gets an error frame plus close 4403 instead of a view.
6. In `crates/server/tests/actor/watch.rs`, inside `mod b50_watching_a_friend`, add `async fn b50_an_uppercase_hello_is_admitted_to_the_friends_live_match` (`#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]`): build like `world_dressed` but with a hex-letter match id — `account`/`befriend`/`start_match(&app, "67e55044-10b1-426f-9247-bb680e5fe0d01", &friend, &rival, false)`, attach both `FakeSocket`s, `settle()`, `serve(&app)`, `connect(WATCH_PATH, &watcher.token)`, send `hello` with `matchId` and `friendId` both `.to_ascii_uppercase()`, then assert `wait_for(0, PROMPTLY, |f| f["type"] == "view")` returns `Some` (mirror `assert_forbidden`'s inverse). Do not reuse `world()`'s id here: `support::store::uuid()` is digits-only, so uppercasing it would be a no-op and the test would pass without the fix.
7. In `crates/server/tests/actor/duos.rs`, inside `mod b35_the_socket`, add two `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]` tests: (a) `b35_an_uppercase_hello_match_id_attaches_to_the_running_actor` — `h.seat(&h.host)` (creates the live actor under the lowercase id), then connect the guest and send `hello(&h.match_id.to_ascii_uppercase())`; (b) `b35_an_uppercase_match_id_query_param_attaches_to_the_running_actor` — after `h.seat(&h.host)`, `connect_offering(&format!("{DUOS_PATH}?matchId={}", upper), &[WS_SUBPROTOCOL, &bearer_protocol(&h.guest.token)])` then send `json!({"type":"hello"})` (no id, so the query value is used). Both start with `assert_ne!(upper, h.match_id, "no hex letters to uppercase")` (server ids are random UUIDs, so this guards a freak digits-only id), then assert the guest gets a view with `seat == "a2"` and the host observes `teammate && connected && !aiPlaying` via `wait_for` (copy the reconnect test near line 1171). Without the fix the guest lands on a duplicate actor (or is refused), and the host is never told the teammate connected.

## Tests

- Unit: `crates/server/src/social/watch.rs` `mod tests` — `a_hello_with_uppercase_ids_is_read_lowercase` (step 4). Run `cargo test -p jackioh-server --lib social::watch::`.
- `crates/server/tests/actor/ws_server.rs` — `an_uppercase_match_id_in_the_query::attaches_to_the_live_match_instead_of_refusing_with_4403` (step 5). Run `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server actor::ws_server::an_uppercase`.
- `crates/server/tests/actor/watch.rs` — `b50_watching_a_friend::b50_an_uppercase_hello_is_admitted_to_the_friends_live_match` (step 6). Run `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server actor::watch::b50_an_uppercase`.
- `crates/server/tests/actor/duos.rs` — both `b35_the_socket::b35_an_uppercase_*` tests (step 7). Run `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server actor::duos::b35_an_uppercase`.
- Existing lowercase behavior is covered by the untouched tests in the same three files; run each file's neighboring tests too (e.g. `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server actor::duos::b35_`).
- Checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`. No `cargo jackioh spec check` (no ruling added).

## Done when

- [ ] Uppercase `?matchId=` on `/ws/match` attaches to the live actor (view arrives, no 4403).
- [ ] Uppercase `matchId`/`friendId` hello on `/ws/watch` is admitted to the live match (no 4403).
- [ ] Uppercase `matchId` in both the duos hello frame and `?matchId=` attach to the existing `DuosActor` (guest sees seat `a2`, host sees teammate connected; no duplicate actor).
- [ ] All-lowercase connections behave as before (neighboring tests green).
- [ ] The three new integration tests plus the unit test fail without the fix (uppercase is a real case change in each: `"MATCH-1"`, a hex-letter UUID, guarded server UUIDs).
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.

## Risks

- The fake store may compare ids by exact string while Postgres casts text to UUID (case-insensitive): normalization happens before every lookup, so both stores see lowercase either way; no store behavior is relied upon.
- No determinism/replay impact: ids are used only as map keys and seat comparisons, never as RNG input; no hidden information is exposed (refusal shape and codes unchanged, per rule 7).
- No new numbers, so rule 9 needs no `config.rs` constant.

## Open questions

None. Every behavior, file, and assertion above is settled by the issue and the code cited; build it as written.
```
